HESPERA / HESTIA — PROTOTYPE WORKING DATA v2.0

CANON: HESPERA = agriculture/growing Application. HESTIA =
physical/local-first growing-control Product operated with/through
HESPERA. GardenOS / GardenOScore = prototype/legacy lineage and
engineering provenance.

RECOVERED PROTOTYPE HISTORY: • early Arduino Uno herb-garden controller.
• DHT22 initially; later DHT11. • soil moisture sensing expanded toward
multiple channels. • PCF8574 introduced for actuator/control expansion.
• LED grow-light control and pump relay control. • project migrated to
Wemos D1 R1/R2 / ESP8266. • ESP8266 single-ADC constraint led to
sensor-line/power-switching experimentation. • confirmed
physical-component family includes DHT11, LM393-type soil-sensor board,
PCF8574 and 5 V relay module. • local web dashboard and JSON API. •
LittleFS configuration/state. • multi-network Wi-Fi direction with
fallback setup AP. • plant database, planter assignment,
rules/presets/custom thresholds. • configuration snapshot/import/export.
• OTA update path. • HomeKit Off / Low Power / Full experiments. •
graph/history and mobile/desktop UI direction. • node architecture
investigated, including PCF8574-based I2C nodes and desire for one-chip
node design. • Core must remain standalone-capable; optional Server
coordinates multiple Cores. • safety of connected hardware remains a
Core responsibility.

IMPORTANT ENGINEERING EVIDENCE: A historical design incorrectly assumed
CD4051 while an on-hand CD4021BE was actually a digital shift register;
that mismatch was identified and corrected in later architecture.
PCF8574 output is suitable for control signalling, not direct
sensor-power supply. Calibration values for moisture/light remain
hardware-specific. Physical wiring, compile and target-board behavior
require evidence before PASS.

CURRENT PRODUCTIZATION GOAL: Translate useful GardenOS prototype
learning into HESPERA/HESTIA without erasing provenance or pretending
legacy prototypes were production-ready.
